name: Die Brucke woodcut
summary: Planks are cut with a few bold gouge strokes, and the grain and the cut marks stay visible. The artists often hand-print on cheap paper with a spoon or a press. The ink is uneven, with flat black masses and sharp angular white.

philosophy.core_thesis: A plank cut with a few hard strokes and printed by hand keeps the cut and the grain. The print shows a raw inner state, not a clean picture.
design_principles: Cut straight into a soft plank with a knife and a gouge; do not draw the picture first in fine detail.
Keep the plank grain and the gouge marks in the print.
Print flat black masses against sharp, angular white shapes.
Add colour from a second or third block in opaque inks such as red and yellow, with 1–3 mm of misregister.
Print by hand with a spoon or a small press, so that the ink covers the sheet unevenly.
Use cheap thin paper, and let the rubbing marks show on the back.
anti_patterns: A soft gradient or a halftone
Exact register of the colour blocks
A clean white margin with no hand marks

process.matrix: Soft plank (pine, plywood), side grain, sometimes cut-up for colour
process.press: Hand-rubbed with spoon or baren, or a small press
process.image_making: Knife and gouge cut straight into the plank; planks sawn apart for colour inking
process.edition: Small editions, 20-100 or monoprinted colour variants

inks.strategy: Black relief ink for the key block, and one to three opaque colour inks that cover the ink under them.

screening.rule: Make each tone as a flat ink mass from one cut; do not screen. Where the cut leaves a grain, let the wood grain print.

registration.rule: Blocks are registered by eye or by pin; the shift of 1–3 mm is a feature of the look.

substrate.stock: Thin Japan, wove or poster paper, grey-cream.
substrate.finish: Thin and slightly rough; it takes the rubbing without a tear.

surface.impression: A deep bite from hand rubbing; the lines show as a relief on the back.
surface.sheen: Matt black, with a slight shine where the ink is thick.
surface.texture: Visible plank grain, jagged cut edges, and an uneven ink film with white speckle.

evidence.title: Poster for the Brucke exhibition, Arnold Gallery Dresden
evidence.credit: Google Art Project, via Wikimedia Commons

emotion.target_response: Raw, urgent tension: the viewer sees angular figures that were cut fast and printed by hand.

use_cases: editorial illustration with a raw edge
avoid_when: The design needs a calm or refined tone.
The text must stay small and exact.

modifiers.how: Cut finer lines that follow the form, print in black only and use laid paper.
Cut each colour on lino with smooth curves and overlap the opaque layers.
